International students board in the same houses as UK students and can join from Year 3 through Year 13, or take the one-year NCUK International Foundation Year. English-language programmes run alongside GCSE, A Level and BTEC study.

name: Ashbourne College
tagline: A selective private GCSE and A level college in Kensington, London, with classes of ten or fewer. Day college: no boarding.
summary: Ashbourne is a small, independently owned college next to Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park, founded in 1981. It teaches GCSEs (Years 10 and 11) and A levels (Years 12 and 13) in classes typically capped at ten, with a weekly personal tutor for each student and a university-style, first-name atmosphere (there is no uniform). Ashbourne is not a boarding school: international students live in hostels, student residences or homestays that the college lists but does not inspect, and students living outside the UK need a UK education guardian.
year_groups: Year 10 to Year 13 (GCSE and A level)

accommodation.summary: No on-site accommodation: Ashbourne is not a boarding school.
notes: The college keeps a list of accommodation providers (student hostels and residences, and homestays with selected families) that students apply to independently.
About 75 students currently live in these arrangements, split roughly evenly between hostels and homestays.
Typical prices are GBP 100 to 700 per week, from shared rooms to self-contained studios, 10 to 30 minutes' journey from the college.
Ashbourne does not inspect these properties or guarantee their standard or safety; families should carry out their own checks.
accommodation.guardianship: Parents of students living outside the UK must appoint a UK-based education guardian with legal authority to act on their behalf (medical care, travel, day-to-day support). The college can provide a list of guardianship and accommodation providers; we can request it for you.

Student visa application fee GBP 348 from outside the UK (paid to the UK government, plus the Immigration Healthcare Surcharge).

name: St Clare's, Oxford (IB)
tagline: England's oldest IB World School: the IB Diploma and a one-to-three-term Pre-IB in North Oxford, with boarding and day places and classes averaging nine students.
summary: St Clare's, Oxford teaches the two-year IB Diploma (ages 16 to 19) and a Pre-IB bridging programme (ages 15 to 16) on a campus of Victorian and Edwardian buildings on the Banbury Road, 1.5 km from Oxford city centre. Students board in 12 houses near the campus, or attend as day students; day students eat with boarders and join every trip and activity. The school is semi-selective, welcomes more than 50 nationalities and has been delivering international education for over 70 years. This record covers the IB school only, not the college's summer, adult or teacher-training courses.
year_groups: Pre-IB (age 15-16) and the two-year IB Diploma (age 16-19)

notes: 12 boarding houses near the campus, typically 16 to 18 students each, every house with a House Parent.
Single, twin and triple rooms; over half of the rooms are en suite. Most boarders share with a student from another country.
Breakfast, lunch and dinner every day, all dietary requirements catered for; house kitchens for snacks.
Weekly boarding exists for a small number of students and is only open to those living in England or Wales (same fee as full boarding).
Day students join boarders for all meals (included in the fee), have lockers and a student hub, and take part in all trips and activities.
All Pre-IB and IB students on a Child Student visa whose parents live overseas must have a nominated UK Educational Guardian.
The college is closed to students during half-term and school holidays (set departure and arrival days apply).

tagline: A boarding and day school for ages 13–18, with GCSE, A Level and a one-year Pre-Sixth Form pathway.

name: Braemar College
tagline: A private Ontario high school and university pathway provider on the University of Toronto campus. Day school with homestay: no boarding house.
summary: Braemar College, founded in 1995, teaches grades 9–12 of the Ontario Secondary School Curriculum in a heritage building on the edge of the University of Toronto’s St. George campus; graduates receive the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD). Its year is made of four nine-week terms, so most students study two courses at a time, and an Express Option allows three. Pathway and Toronto Pathway programmes prepare students for Canadian universities and colleges, with official partnerships with the University of Toronto, York, Waterloo and Toronto Metropolitan University. Braemar is not a boarding school: international students live with Braemar-vetted homestay families.

accommodation.summary: No boarding house: international students normally live in a Braemar homestay. Residence places exist only subject to seasonal availability.
notes: Homestay families provide a private furnished room, wifi and three meals a day. Published price: $400 CAD per week plus a $300 placement fee.
Families are visited in person before joining the programme, re-inspected every three years, and every adult in the household needs a valid criminal record check or vulnerable sector scan.
Most homestays are 30–50 minutes from the school by public transport (TTC). The school is downtown, surrounded mainly by apartments and condos.

Minimum homestay is three months (12 weeks) for standard programmes; if paid in advance, the first three months are not refundable once the study permit is approved. Students may change homestay without notice during the first two weeks; afterwards two weeks’ notice is required.
Students are encouraged to arrive the week before classes. Weekday flights landing after 5 pm are preferred so the family is home.
accommodation.guardianship: Students under 18 who need custodianship services through Braemar must also submit a signed custodianship form for notarization, and these services are provided only to students staying in a Braemar homestay. The $200 notarization fee is non-refundable if the study permit is refused.

name: Delta School District International Programs
tagline: Seven public secondary schools for grades 8–12 near Vancouver (Burnsview, Delta, Delview, North Delta, Sands, Seaquam, South Delta), with a district-run homestay and custodianship program. Day schools: no boarding.
summary: Delta School District International Programs places international students in one of seven public secondary schools across the communities of Tsawwassen, Ladner and North Delta, a short drive from downtown Vancouver and its airport. Students follow the British Columbia curriculum taught by certified BC teachers, with ESL instruction included in tuition and an international coordinator at every school; Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate and French Immersion options are available at some schools. International students normally live in the district’s own homestay program, run by school district staff rather than a private business, which also provides custodianship and airport pick-up. Students apply to the district and choose a school by community, size and timetable system.

accommodation.summary: No boarding houses: international students normally live in the district’s own homestay program, run by school district staff rather than a private business.
notes: Host families are screened with a criminal record check, interviewed and inspected. Students get a private bedroom with a bed, study table and lamp, bathroom and laundry facilities, three meals a day and snacks, in a home where English is the main language.
Transport assistance is provided if the school is more than a 20-minute walk away. Airport pick-up and drop-off is free for homestay students.
Students describe their needs on the application. Once matched, they receive a profile with photos and contact details so they can get in touch before arrival.

Each area has a homestay coordinator (Tsawwassen; Delta and Delview; Seaquam and Burnsview; North Delta and Sands), backed by the Homestay Manager and cultural support staff, with 24-hour emergency contact and care.
Students must give host families at least two weeks’ notice before moving out, or pay two weeks.
Published homestay price: $1,350 per month in the 2027–28 fee sheet, plus a $500 annual management fee.
accommodation.guardianship: District custodianship is provided for students in the district homestay ($500); private custodianship is also accepted for homestay students. Students may instead live with parents, family or family friends, or use a private homestay and custodianship company. For parents living in Delta the district runs orientations and meet-and-greets and refers them to rental resources; parents who need custodian documents for IRCC pay a one-time $200.

district_schools.name: Burnsview Secondary School
district_schools.summary: A smaller school with high academic standards and strong student achievement. It keeps a wide range of options, from the sciences and Robotics to the Arts and Applied Skills, with very active student leadership groups, clubs and sports teams, and a focus on connectedness and on self-regulating, academically engaged students.

image.alt: Front entrance of Burnsview Secondary School in North Delta

district_schools.name: Delta Secondary School
district_schools.summary: In the historic farming and fishing community of Ladner, and home to the 400-seat Genesis Theatre for school and community performances. Programs and activities cover academics, business, culinary arts, fine and performing arts, applied design and skills technology, and athletics, with a wide range of teams, clubs and courses. The school says about 90% of its students speak English as a first language.

image.alt: Entrance of Delta Secondary School in Ladner

district_schools.name: Delview Secondary School
district_schools.summary: The smallest secondary school in the district, in the heart of North Delta, with a personal approach and a caring staff focused on connection, engagement and mental health and wellness. A 35-minute flex block four days a week lets students reach teachers, finish work or follow their own projects. Facilities include a large gymnasium, fitness centre, updated computer labs, a media arts room and a woodwork shop, with a community recreation centre nearby.

image.alt: Front entrance of Delview Secondary School in North Delta

district_schools.name: North Delta Secondary School
district_schools.summary: A mainly semestered school in a more urban area, with a diverse, multicultural and inclusive community. The semester system gives flexibility to students who arrive mid-year. Courses span the Sciences, Mathematics, Social Studies, Language Arts, Physical Education, Applied Skills, Modern Languages and Fine and Performing Arts, and the school is well known for its athletics program across the fall, winter and spring seasons.

image.alt: Front of North Delta Secondary School

district_schools.name: Sands Secondary School
district_schools.summary: A small school in a suburban part of North Delta with a comfortable, intimate campus and more personal attention. Its student leadership body promotes social responsibility and a global vision (motto: “Creating Our Future Today”). FLEX time four days a week lets students choose extra support, and extra-curricular options include athletics, clubs, Student Council and the District Youth Advisory Council.

image.alt: Entrance of Sands Secondary School with the Canadian flag

district_schools.name: Seaquam Secondary School
district_schools.summary: A strong tradition of academic excellence, with graduates winning scholarships and bursaries at universities across Canada and the United States. Seaquam offers the IB program, a wide selection of Fine Arts and Career programs, and many athletics teams, clubs and outside activities in a pleasant North Delta community.

image.alt: Seaquam Secondary School main building and athletic centre

district_schools.name: South Delta Secondary School
district_schools.schedule: Mainly linear; some grade 12 academic subjects on semester
district_schools.summary: In the small, safe, family community of Tsawwassen, close to beaches, golf courses and parks. Students show consistently strong academic results. The school offers AP, French Immersion, academics, applied skills and fine arts, a renowned Musical Theatre program that stages a Broadway-style musical each year, and sports teams (the Sundevils) that the school describes as among the strongest in the province, plus clubs including Student Council, Interact and downhill skiing.

image.alt: South Delta Secondary School building in Tsawwassen

district_schools_note: All seven are public secondary schools offering ESL instruction, counsellors and an international coordinator. Populations are rounded and differ between sources; confirm current figures and the timetable with the school. Students choose a school by community, size and timetable system.
facilities: Genesis Theatre, a 400-seat theatre, at Delta Secondary
Large gymnasium, fitness centre, computer labs, media arts room and woodwork shop at Delview
Teaching cafeteria and Film and Television Production Academy at South Delta
Specialized, up-to-date indoor and outdoor facilities at every secondary school
highlights: Seven public secondary schools, grades 8–12, across Tsawwassen, Ladner and North Delta: Burnsview, Delta, Delview, North Delta, Sands, Seaquam and South Delta
District-run homestay and custodianship with 24-hour support
ESL instruction included in tuition and an international coordinator at every school
Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate and French Immersion options
Monthly supervised sightseeing activities and a University Fair every November
review_flags: Populations differ across sources: Delta Secondary shows 1,500 students and 125 international in its facts but about 1,400 and 120 in its text; North Delta shows 1,400 on the website, about 1,300 in its text and 1,200 in the brochures. Website figures were used.
The Delta Secondary page lists no AP courses; AP comes from the 2024 brochure. Academies, course counts and sports lists appear only in the 2019 brochure and were not imported.
The fee sheet is for 2027–28 (updated February 2026). The host-family page lists homestay at $1,300 per month from September 2026, against $1,350 on the fee sheet.
The fee sheet has no price for short-term, graduation or summer programs, or for students not in homestay; none was imported.
Only the seven secondary schools (grades 8–12) were imported. Elementary schools (24, Kindergarten to Grade 7), summer programs and the Graduation program are not covered.

Seven building photos come from the district’s own Secondary Schools page (publication permission not verified). Delta Secondary is used as the district hero and card image. No age range, gender policy or founding date is published for the district; left empty.
Fees are in Canadian dollars with no conversion; fee sorting leaves the yearly figure empty for this reason.
